name: Square
description: Protects against destructive Square CLI/API operations like deleting catalog objects \ or customers (which can break payment flows).

destructive_patterns.name: square-catalog-delete
destructive_patterns.description: square catalog delete removes catalog objects, impacting products and inventory.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting catalog objects removes products, variations, modifiers, or categories \ from your Square catalog. POS systems, online stores, and invoicing that \ reference these items will show errors or missing products.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - square catalog list to review items first \ - Set item visibility to hidden instead of deleting \ - Export catalog backup before bulk deletions

destructive_patterns.name: square-api-delete-catalog-object
destructive_patterns.description: Square API DELETE /v2/catalog/object/{id} deletes a catalog object.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Direct API deletion of catalog objects bypasses CLI safety checks. Products, \ categories, taxes, discounts, and modifiers can be permanently removed, \ breaking POS workflows and e-commerce integrations.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /v2/catalog/object/{id} to verify before deletion \ - Use batch operations with careful ID validation \ - Test in Square sandbox environment first

destructive_patterns.name: square-api-batch-delete-catalog-objects
destructive_patterns.description: Square API POST /v2/catalog/batch-delete deletes multiple catalog objects.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Batch deleting catalog objects can remove up to 200 products, variations, \ modifiers, categories, or related objects in one call. Deletion cascades to \ dependent catalog objects, so a wrong ID list can remove more than the \ immediate targets.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Retrieve and review every object ID before deletion \ - Export a catalog backup before batch deletion \ - Test the request against Square sandbox first

destructive_patterns.name: square-api-delete-customer
destructive_patterns.description: Square API DELETE /v2/customers/{id} deletes a customer.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Square customer removes their profile, cards on file, and loyalty \ data. Transaction history loses customer context, affecting reporting and \ CRM. Repeat customers will need to re-register.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - GET /v2/customers/{id} to verify customer before deletion \ - Remove cards on file instead of full deletion \ - Export customer data before deletion for compliance

destructive_patterns.name: square-api-delete-payment-link
destructive_patterns.description: Square API DELETE /v2/online-checkout/payment-links/{id} deletes a payment link.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a Square payment link cancels the associated checkout order and makes \ the shared link unusable. Customers who already received the link cannot pay \ through it after deletion.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Retrieve the payment link and order before deletion \ - Deactivate or replace the link intentionally through Square Dashboard \ - Notify customers before invalidating a shared checkout link

destructive_patterns.name: square-api-delete-location
destructive_patterns.description: Square API DELETE /v2/locations/{id} deletes a location.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a location removes a business location from Square. This affects \ payment processing, inventory tracking, and employee management for that \ location. Transactions cannot be processed at a deleted location.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Set location status to inactive instead of deleting \ - GET /v2/locations/{id} to verify location details first \ - Transfer inventory and employees before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: square-api-delete-webhook-subscription
destructive_patterns.description: Square API DELETE /v2/webhooks/subscriptions/{id} deletes a webhook subscription.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a webhook subscription stops event notifications for payments, \ refunds, inventory changes, and other business events. Your application \ will miss critical updates until the subscription is recreated.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - Disable the webhook subscription instead of deleting \ - GET /v2/webhooks/subscriptions to verify subscription ID \ - Set up backup notification channels before removal
